notes: Evaluation focused on low-latency inline completions for their cloud IDE. Key asks: TTFT 80-120ms (editor inline), 95th percentile tail <200ms; jitter tolerated <30ms. Token budget per suggestion typically 12-40 tokens for single-line completions, up to 120 tokens for multi-line snippets. Concerned about backpressure when user types rapidly and editor queue grows — want automatic graceful degradation (fallback to cached prefix or smaller local model). Interested in model pinning for stable UX across releases; worried about hidden regressions from upstream model updates. Security: absolute requirement for VPC/private control plane for source code IP, SSO/SAML + audit logs + KMS integration. Cost sensitivity: looking to shave per-developer monthly inference costs via batching + token budget tuning; Optimize feature suggestions are attractive. POC plan: run branch-level microbench (warm vs cold KV cache), simulate 1000 concurrent editors, measure TTFT median/95/99, end-to-end jitter, and tokens/sec. Notes from call: "If TTFT spikes, developers abandon the suggestion — first token is everything." AE captured desire to prefer smaller quantized models for quick inline, escalate to larger models for long refactors. SE requested sample telemetry schema and suggested prefix cache hit metric.
